root_cause.hypothesis: All unhealthy targets are concentrated in a single Availability Zone (ap-south-1a), with ap-south-1b and ap-south-1c fully healthy. Combined with target-level timeouts and failed health checks, this points to an AZ-localized infrastructure impairment (network path, AZ capacity, or underlying host issue) rather than a bad deploy or target-group/LB config change, since no changes were recorded in either in the 6h window.
ruled_out: Target group or load balancer configuration change (C2, C3 show no changes in 6h)
Uniform/global unhealthiness across all AZs (M8-M11 show 1b and 1c are fully healthy)

proposal.reasoning: All 3 unhealthy targets are isolated to ap-south-1a while ap-south-1b and ap-south-1c are fully healthy (M6-M11). The load balancer supports zonal_shift (C9), making AZ traffic shift the safest immediate mitigation while the AZ-level issue is investigated, since no target group or LB config changes explain the failures.
proposal.expected_effect: Traffic is routed away from the impaired ap-south-1a zone to the healthy ap-south-1b and ap-south-1c targets, restoring overall service health and reducing 5xx errors and timeouts.
